newsitem.title: USA: Stocks drift lower, investors cautious.
newsitem.headline: Stocks drift lower, investors cautious.

text.p: Stock prices were lower Thursday, reflecting Wall Street's cautious tone after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning over the market's lofty levels.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 20.78 points at 6,962.40 adding to Wednesday's loss of 55 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on volume of about 246 million shares.
"Greenspan's comments put a tremor back into the market," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray.

The wary trading came after the Fed chief, delivering his semi-annual report on the economy to the Senate on Wednesday, spoke in surprisingly blunt terms of his concerns about the risks of inflation as well as the dramatic increase in stock prices.
Greenspan's comments, coupled with a lower bond market sapped buyers' enthusiasm, analysts said.
A $6.6 billion merger between computer networking company 3Com Corp. and modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp. failed to breathe life into beleaguered high technology stocks.
3Com fell 3 to 36 and U.S. Robotics rose 2 to 63 on news of their proposed merger.
Tech stocks are suffering through a traditionally weak time of the year for the group, and is also the focus of profit taking by momentum investors, analysts said.
"The tech sector is very weak," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management. "The tide is going out on them. A lot of investors who had gains are cutting them back."

Bonds were hurt by a stronger-than-expected increase of 3.6 percent in durable goods orders for January compared with a revised fall of 1.8 percent in December. Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a rise of 1.5 percent.
On the bond market, the closely-watched 30-year Treasury bond was off a quarter point, which raised its yield to 6.79 percent from Wednesday's close of 6.78 percent.
Analysts said they did not think it was likely that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates soon, despite Greenspan's warning about the dangers of the stock market's strength.
But they said they expected stocks to slip into a trading range over the next few weeks as investors step back to assess their positions.
"The market leaders are up so much this year that I think some sort of consolidation or modest correction phase is probably going to take place," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at JC Bradford.
Among other computer networking stocks, Cisco Systems Inc. fell 1-1/2 to 56-5/8, Ascend Communications Inc. lost 3 to 59-3/8 and Cascade Communications Corp. fell 1 to 31-5/8.
Gold stocks rallied with the price of the precious metal. On New York's Commodity Exchange, April gold was up $6.70 at $362.70 an ounce.
Newmont Mining Corp. rose 1-3/8 to 47-1/8, Homestake Mining Co. added 5/8 to 16-5/8, Getchell Gold Corp. rose 2-3/8 to 48-3/4.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 8.61 points at 1,331.94. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.67 to 596.64.
